caption:
🎾 Grand Slam singles titles, country by country — 1905 → 2025.

The United States takes the lead in 1919 and ends on 323 titles. Part of it is the calendar: when the world wars stop the other majors, the US Championships keep going, so American titles keep ticking while almost everyone else freezes 🗽 Australia climbs from 48 to 112 between 1946 and 1965, its post-war golden age. And Switzerland goes from 7 to 30 between 2000 and 2018: the Federer years.

📊 Data: Wikipedia, from the four majors' official records (CC BY-SA). Men's and women's singles combined; each title goes to the country the champion represented that year.
